bug_semantics: An attacker-influenced date-format argument can contain an arbitrarily large numeric strftime width such as %5000000d. The strftime parser captures that width, forwards it without a bound or resource charge to padStart(), and the historical pad() implementation prepends one character per iteration. A tiny template therefore drives attacker-sized output, repeated string copying, CPU consumption, and possible OOM while bypassing configured memoryLimit accounting and renderLimit checkpoints.
flaw_origin: Commit ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759 added full strftime width syntax in src/util/strftime.ts: rFormat began capturing (\d+)?, format() assigned the capture to padWidth, and padStart(ret, padWidth, padChar) consumed it unchecked. The same commit refactored src/util/underscore.ts into a generic pad() whose while (n-- > 0) loop repeatedly concatenated strings. The existing src/builtin/filters/date.ts passed its format argument to strftime, while src/template/filter/filter.ts evaluated filter arguments against Context, completing the attacker-controlled path.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author harttle <yangjvn@126.com> and committer harttle <yangjvn@126.com>; its subject/body contain no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/security/advisories/GHSA-hh27-hf48-9f5q identifies the unchecked numeric width path through src/util/strftime.ts to padStart()/pad() in src/util/underscore.ts, demonstrates {{ d | date: f }} with f=%5000000d exceeding memoryLimit and renderLimit, and declares affected versions <=10.25.7.

git log -L 133,147:src/util/strftime.ts at pre-fix commit 5b9c3469085e01c79e2d0af28e2a13f730e1793d traces the vulnerable width destructuring, padWidth assignment, and padStart call to ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759; git log -S'let padWidth = width' independently identifies that commit as the original addition rather than later type/refactor commits.

The BIC diff at https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/commit/ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759 adds const rFormat = /%([-_0^#:]+)?(\d+)?([EO])?(.)/, passes width through format(), computes padWidth = width || padWidths[conversion] || 0, calls padStart(ret, padWidth, padChar), and introduces the generic per-character pad() loop in src/util/underscore.ts.

Direct-parent tree verification of c69ad538d48f3cd52c6147da653b9d3e47dfd043:src/util/strftime.ts shows only /%./g parsing at lines 166-182 and fixed-width conversion helpers; it has no numeric-width capture, no width/padWidth variables, and no path from a format width to padStart. Thus the vulnerable lines/mechanism are absent in the immediate parent.

At the BIC, src/builtin/filters/date.ts directly calls strftime(date, arg), and src/template/filter/filter.ts evaluates each filter argument with Expression(arg).evaluate(context), proving that a context-controlled format reaches the newly added width parser rather than merely an internal hard-coded caller.

Tag-boundary history shows ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759 first contained by v9.6.0 (tag commit 5ec3f95317e78a1d0ae8866c7f8cbf18ea8a9263); the v9.5.0-to-v9.6.0 diff adds the width regex and unchecked padWidth flow, while v9.5.0 (90d78ae6d573e977478920f81d2af0a56da88011) lacks it. The mechanism persists through v10.25.7 (34877950bfd0f88666f4ef61f7704defdea546b0), consistent with the advisory's upper bound; repository history therefore supplies the more precise lower boundary v9.6.0.

Advisory-linked fix https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/commit/3129d46dc95efa357b00e5a57ee1af80a13d72ed directly threads Context.memoryLimit from src/filters/date.ts into strftime, charges Number(padWidth)-ret.length before padding in src/util/strftime.ts, and replaces src/util/underscore.ts's repeated one-character loop with ch.repeat(n) plus one concatenation.

git tag --contains 3129d46dc95efa357b00e5a57ee1af80a13d72ed starts at v10.26.0 and excludes v10.25.7. The first-party v10.26.0 release at https://github.com/harttle/liquidjs/releases/tag/v10.26.0 explicitly lists this full fix commit; the v10.26.0 tree contains the pre-allocation memory charge and the tag points to c20c0af02d33e8d2ca6b08925eadca8755257c39. Although the advisory UI says 'Patched versions None', its <=10.25.7 range, fix reference, release note, and tag-tree content prove v10.26.0 as the repository's fixed boundary.

Exact BIC-object inspection (git show --format=raw ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759) shows one parent, human author/committer harttle <yangjvn@126.com>, and no trailers or AI markers. AI attribution was decided solely from this BIC object; no squash decomposition was needed.
reasoning: The causal defect begins when ba5ff3f41c61acc2c3668ae2bbcc48dd168b1759 makes decimal width text in a date format control the number of padding iterations with no bound. Earlier fixed-width padStart calls are not the same vulnerability: the immediate parent cannot parse %5000000d as a width, whereas the BIC both recognizes the width and routes it into the concatenating loop. Context-evaluated filter arguments make that new data flow reachable from attacker-influenced render data. The vulnerable flow survives later moves and refactors and is present at v10.25.7. Commit 3129d46dc95efa357b00e5a57ee1af80a13d72ed is the direct remediation because it charges the requested padding before allocation and removes per-character concatenation; it first ships in v10.26.0. The BIC is a single-parent ordinary commit, not a move, revert, merge, release commit, or squash aggregate requiring decomposition. Its exact commit object has human identities and no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI even though AI signals on any later commit would be irrelevant.
